text:
Cam Fowler is 34, more than 1,100 games into a career that started in Anaheim, and in his second full season as a Blue that role is narrowing. His ice time is down 2.2 minutes over his last ten games, to about 19.5, and he has no goals and six assists in 23 games after scoring 30 points last season.

The underlying picture is middling rather than alarming. St. Louis gets about half of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, close to the team rate. Our range expects about 25 points.

He still does the things that made him a first-round pick in 2010. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting with possession 56% of the time last season and carrying the puck in on 42% of his entries; carry-ins produced a chance 25% of the time in tracked games, dump-ins 8%. The cost, per Evolving-Hockey, was defense: opponents got noticeably more with him on the ice, bottom 6% of defensemen, and they had him around replacement level overall. The Blues have won six of their last ten, with him in a quieter role.
